jobs.description: At Amazon Ads, we're re-imagining the advertising landscape through advanced generative AI technologies and AI agents, revolutionizing how millions of customers discover products and engage with brands online. jobs.description: AWS Corporate Strategy & Business Development – North America Emerging Companies, Supplier & Vendor Portfolio AWS is seeking a Corporate Strategy and Business Development leader to join our team with a focus on AWSI Deep Engagements across our North America emerging company customers within Amazon's Supplier & Vendor portfolio. This role will drive holistic strategies across Amazon's business with high-potential emerging partners and suppliers, working at the intersection of AWS and broader Amazon. This is a unique opportunity to join a centralized corporate team that manages strategic partnerships across all of Amazon with an AWS lens. The companies we work with are among Amazon's most promising emerging suppliers and vendors, and this role will help them drive technology transformation via AWS tools, technology, and partners. AWS and Amazon are on the forefront of the AI revolution with partners and the companies building the future of supply chain, commerce, and vendor innovation. We are seeking a person who can continuously (and effectively) walk the line between thought leader and executor, every day. The person will be responsible for assessing inbound requests, independently managing opportunities end-to-end (commonly the most complex challenges in never-been-done-before deals), and seeing complex and high-impact partnerships through to completion. An in-depth knowledge of how emerging companies operate within Amazon's Supplier & Vendor ecosystem, how they engage across Amazon, and what Amazon's strategy is (or could be) with these types of companies is important. The person will need a strong commercial aptitude and be able to quickly identify best-in-class partnerships that are valuable and high-impact for Amazon, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and our customers. You'll also manage executive relationships and negotiate partnership deals that are unconventional, need a centralized advocate, and/or have broader implications to AWS and other Amazon business units that are not immediately obvious. This includes non-standard deal construction, complex accounting procedures, and deal negotiations that require creative problem-solving and deep commercial expertise. This role will interact closely with internal AWS and Amazon leaders from various disciplines, requiring confidence and credibility when engaging with the most senior leadership at both AWS and Amazon. This key role will be highly visible at senior levels of the organization and work on some of our most vexing challenges. You will need to work collaboratively with internal management teams to understand relative advantages and risks, if/when major features should be included to existing roadmaps, consolidation, and adoption. You'll at times need to be comfortable moving forward without a clear path, almost always with high degrees of ambiguity. Communication & Writing This role demands exceptional written and oral communication skills. You will regularly author strategy documents, build executive-level presentations, and communicate complex partnership narratives to senior leaders. Effective communication (written and verbal) at the executive level is not a nice-to-have; it is core to the role. Travel & Availability This role requires willingness to travel within North America, sometimes with little notice. While travel may reach 75% during peak deal cycles, the typical expectation is approximately 25%, depending on engagement cadence. While we strive for a healthy work-life balance, the highly visible nature of this role and the types of deals we work on mean it is not unusual to work well outside of normal hours, including weekends. The Ideal Candidate We are seeking an analytical, technical, and strategic thinker who is passionate and relentless. The ideal candidate enjoys solving complex problems where there is no clearly defined path to success, and isn't frustrated by a lack of clarity when defining how to execute. This individual must be able to work effectively with cross-functional teams and thrives in a fast-paced setting that is constantly evolving and isn't dissuaded when they hear "no" or frustrated by shifting priorities. Experience working with emerging and high-growth companies, particularly within supplier, vendor, or marketplace ecosystems, is highly valued. Finally, as our deals are atypical, we require a leader who is comfortable defining goals that align to the right business outcomes, and is exceptionally comfortable driving the right outcomes with little guidance. Key job responsibilities Identify, evaluate, and manage strategic partnership opportunities with North America emerging companies across Amazon's Supplier & Vendor portfolio, driving technology transformation through AWS tools, technology, and partners. Independently manage complex, end-to-end deal cycles including non-standard deal construction, creative accounting procedures, and unconventional partnership structures with no established playbook. Engage with senior leadership at AWS and Amazon, presenting partnership strategies spanning multiple business units including ASCS, Amazon Ads, and Amazon Stores. Negotiate high-impact partnership agreements requiring a centralized advocate, including co-selling and co-innovation opportunities with suppliers and vendors to Amazon. Author strategy documents, executive-level presentations, and written narratives articulating complex partnership opportunities, risks, and recommendations. Assess inbound requests from emerging suppliers and vendors, prioritize by strategic value and multi-BU potential, and determine engagement models across lead sharing, co-selling, and co-innovation. Collaborate cross-functionally across AWS and Amazon to evaluate advantages, risks, roadmap implications, and adoption strategies. Travel within North America (typically 25%, up to 75% during peak periods), sometimes with limited notice. Navigate ambiguity with evolving priorities and first-of-their-kind deal structures involving high-growth emerging companies. A day in the life A day in the life involves navigating complex, multi-stakeholder relationships across AWS and Amazon. You'll engage directly with C-suite executives at some of AWS' largest customers, aligning their technology transformation goals with AWS capabilities. Internally, you'll collaborate with account teams, service teams, and Amazon business leaders to build holistic strategies that unlock value across the entire Amazon relationship. No two days look alike, you may be negotiating a non-standard deal structure in the morning and authoring an executive strategy document by afternoon. About the team Diverse Experiences AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying. Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud offering. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating. That's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our broad suite of products and services to power their businesses. Inclusive Team Culture Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness. Mentorship & Career Growth We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

jobs.description: Job Summary: CLIENT DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR Location : Preference for candidate to be based in a major city on the West Coast such as Phoenix, Las Vegas, Salt Lake City, Denver, San Francisco, Seattle, etc. Division : Ticketmaster Line Manager: EVP, Head of Sports Contract Terms: Permanent, Full-Time, 40 hours per week WHO WE ARE We’re fans who help fans everywhere get in to the live events they love. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role
As a TPU Kernel Engineer, you'll be responsible for identifying and addressing performance issues across many different ML systems, including research, training, and inference. A significant portion of this work will involve designing and optimizing kernels for the TPU. You will also provide feedback to researchers about how model changes impact performance. Strong candidates will have a track record of solving large-scale systems problems and low-level optimization.
You may be a good fit if you:
Have significant experience optimizing ML systems for TPUs, GPUs, or other accelerators
Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Pick up slack, even if it goes outside your job description
Enjoy pair programming (we love to pair!)
Want to learn more about machine learning research
Care about the societal impacts of your work
Strong candidates may also have experience with:
High performance, large-scale ML systems
Designing and implementing kernels for TPUs or other ML accelerators
Understanding accelerators at a deep level, e.g. a background in computer architecture
ML framework internals
Language modeling with transformers
Representative projects:
Implement low-latency, high-throughput sampling for large language models
Adapt existing models for low-precision inference
Build quantitative models of system performance
Design and implement custom collective communication algorithms
Debug kernel performance at the assembly level

Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.
TEAM OVERVIEW
The Global Security & Operational Resilience team provides 24/7 support across the Firm’s global operations, helping protect people, assets, and the continuity of critical business services. The ~80-member global team drives readiness through integrated physical security and investigations, threat and intelligence monitoring, crisis management, and enterprise operational resilience planning, exercising, and response.
POSITION SUMMARY
KKR is seeking a
principal-level Head of Operational Resilience
to lead the design, implementation, and execution of the firm’s global Operational Resilience program. Reporting to the
Head of Security and Operational Resilience
, this role is responsible for driving accountability and adherence to impact tolerance and recovery objectives during severe and plausible disruption by embedding requirements into day-to-day operations, operating effective controls, and leading remediation efforts to closure.
This role partners closely with
Technology
,
Business leadership
,
Enterprise Risk Management
,
Compliance

Vendor management

, and
Internal Audit
to maintain alignment with client, investor, and regulatory expectations and enterprise risk standards.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Key responsibilities include:
Leadership & Operating Model
Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing operational resilience team.
Influence cross-functional stakeholders to deliver enterprise resilience outcomes and measurable program maturity.
Program Ownership & Roadmap
Own and operate KKR’s Operational Resilience program and multi-year roadmap, including associated procedures, playbooks, and evidence management.
Establish and maintain governance routines to track progress, escalate risks, and drive timely decision-making.
Important Business Services & Impact Tolerances
Identify, maintain, and periodically review the inventory of Important Business Services (IBS) and support dependencies across people, processes, technology, data, facilities, and third parties.
Define, document, and operationalize IBS impact tolerances with business leaders; ensure tolerances are measurable, actionable, and embedded in operating procedures and controls.
Scenario Testing & Exercising
Design and execute severe but plausible scenario testing and resilience exercises to validate the ability to remain within impact tolerances and recovery time objectives.
Document outcomes, lessons learned, and resulting control enhancements; ensure improvements are implemented and sustained.
Business Continuity Management
Own and oversee the Business Continuity Management (BCM) program, including plan development, certification, governance, training/awareness, testing/exercises, and event execution.
Control Effectiveness & Remediation
Identify resilience gaps and drive remediation to closure with clear accountability, milestones, and risk transparency.
Track remediation progress through governance forums and management reporting.
Integrated Response & Recovery
Coordinate resilience integration across crisis management, cyber incident response, technology disaster recovery, and physical security response to enable a unified enterprise response and recovery capability.
Metrics, Reporting & Communication
Establish and maintain resilience KPIs/KRIs, dashboards, and management reporting to communicate posture, key risks, and remediation status to senior leadership.
Lead preparedness, communications, and awareness initiatives to strengthen resilience culture and improve adoption of planning and control requirements across global functions.
Audit, Risk, and Regulatory Support
Support regulatory reviews, risk assessments, and internal/external audits by providing timely documentation, evidence, and program narratives.
QUALIFICATIONS
10+ years of experience in operational resilience, business continuity, enterprise risk, or related disciplines; experience in financial services or similarly regulated environments preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-level resilience initiatives and driving cross-functional delivery in a global organization.
Strong understanding of global regulatory expectations and industry standards (e.g., Basel, ISO 22301, NIST, PRA/FCA or comparable).
Experience engaging with senior leadership during disruption events and managing complex stakeholder environments.
Sector knowledge/experience in Insurance, Asset Management, Capital Markets, and Structuring processes.
CRITICAL COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS
Executive presence with the ability to communicate resilience posture, trade-offs, and decisions clearly to senior leaders.
Strong stakeholder management and influence across Technology, business functions, and control partners (ERM, Compliance, Audit).
Program and change leadership: ability to build roadmaps, drive adoption, and deliver measurable outcomes across a global organization.
Analytical rigor and diligence; ability to translate complex dependencies into practical controls and recovery strategies.
Decisive leadership under pressure, including crisis response coordination and effective prioritization during disruption events.
Strong writing and documentation capability; comfortable producing defensible evidence for audits and regulatory reviews.
Continuous improvement orientation, including process enhancement, tooling modernization, and operational discipline.
